evidence: Consolidated 2023/1542 as of 13.08.2026 (https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02023R1542-20260813; amended only by M1 2024/1781, M2 2025/1561, M3 2026/1738): Art 13(1)-(3) 'From 18 August 2026 or 18 months after the date of entry into force of the implementing act referred to in paragraph 10, whichever is the latest'; Art 13(10) 'The Commission shall, by 18 August 2025, adopt implementing acts to establish harmonised specifications for the labelling requirements'. Cellar SPARQL (publications.europa.eu/webapi/rdf/sparql) of all acts based on / citing / amending 32023R1542 dated 2025-01-01 onward (latest hit: 52026XC05531 of 22.10.2026) and a title search ('batter' + 'label'/'2023/1542') show no Art 13(10) labelling implementing act; only 2025/2289 (reporting), 2026/1770 (removability), 2026/2048 (harmonised standard). dpp-tool.com/en/guide/eu-battery-regulation/ says not published as of 22 Oct 2026. Art 95(c) 'Article 21(2) until 18 August 2026'. Note: the row sits under '1. 이미 적용 중인 날짜'; the new text says it does not apply yet, so whoever applies it should move the row to '2. 앞으로 적용될 날짜' (as the reviewer's problem text says).

Same as #1: Art 13(1)-(3), (10) text in https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02023R1542-20260813 is unchanged, and Cellar SPARQL as of 2026-10-26 lists no implementing act on the Art 13(10) labelling specifications. Since 18 Aug 2026 has passed, the date is now 18 months after that act enters into force.

https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1770: 'Official Journal of the European Union L series 2026/1770 22.10.2026 COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2026/1770 of 14 July 2026 ... as regards derogations for the removability and replaceability of portable batteries'; Art 1 'Article 11(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 is replaced by the following: ... (a) appliances, including wearable devices, specifically designed to operate primarily in an environment that is regularly subject to splashing water ... (c) wearable devices for which the safety, durability, or water resistance may be compromised by user access to the battery and which: (i) ... too small ... or (ii) rely on a compact, sealed enclosure ... (d) until 31 July 2030, electric toys that incorporate rechargeable batteries. when, due to the nature or size of the toy, the derogation is necessary to ensure the safety of the toy ... (e) wireless thermometer probes specifically designed for food contact during food preparation processes; (f) products falling within the scope of Article 1 of Directive 2014/34/EU; (g) on-body delivery systems specifically designed for the subcutaneous administration of medicinal products; (h) telematics devices intended for roof-mounted installation in agricultural and construction machinery ... The derogations set out in points (a), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g) and (h) ... shall only be applicable where such derogation is required to ensure the safety of the user and the appliance.' Art 2: in force on the 20th day after publication = 11 Nov 2026. Act number, title, OJ date and entry into force all confirmed. Correction: the proposed text adds plain '웨어러블 기기', which is broader than the act. Wearables get the exception only (a) as water-exposed washable appliances or (c) when they are too small or rely on a sealed enclosure, so that user access would compromise safety, durability or water resistance. The toy condition is also missing. The closing note is made specific to Art 11(2), because the Art 11(3) sentence follows in the doc.
new: <li>분리·교체 의무의 예외: 물에 정기적으로 노출되고 세척 가능한 기기(안전상 필요한 경우에 한함), 전문가용 의료 영상·방사선 치료 기기와 체외진단 의료기기는 독립 전문가만 교체하도록 설계할 수 있습니다(제11조(2)). 위임규정 (EU) 2026/1770(2026년 10월 22일 관보 게재, 2026년 11월 11일 발효)은 제11조(2)를 바꿔 예외를 넓혔습니다. 물에 노출되는 기기에 웨어러블 기기도 포함된다고 명시했고, 다음 제품을 더했습니다: 너무 작거나 밀폐 구조에 의존해서 사용자가 배터리에 손대면 안전·내구성·방수가 손상될 수 있는 웨어러블 기기, 충전식 배터리가 든 전기 장난감(2030년 7월 31일까지, 장난감의 성격이나 크기상 안전에 필요한 경우), 조리 중 식품에 닿는 무선 온도계 프로브, 폭발 위험 장소용 기기(지침 2014/34/EU 적용 대상), 피하 투약용 신체 부착형 주입 장치, 농업·건설 기계 지붕에 다는 텔레매틱스 기기. 의료 기기를 뺀 예외는 모두 사용자와 기기의 안전에 필요한 경우에만 적용됩니다. 아래 제11조 번역의 제2항은 개정 전 문안입니다.

evidence: https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1703: 'Official Journal of the European Union L series 2026/1703 10.7.2026 REGULATION (EU) 2026/1703 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 8 July 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1157 as regards the prohibition on the export of mixed municipal waste destined for recovery'; Art 1 'In Article 44(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1157, point (f) is replaced by the following: "(f) the export of waste referred to in Article 4(3) shall be prohibited, except to Switzerland;"'; Art 2: in force on the 20th day after publication = 30 July 2026. Art 44 of 2024/1157 (https://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1157) is the 'General regime for exports of waste' for recovery to OECD-Decision countries, and Recital 1 of 2026/1703 confirms point (f) is the mixed municipal waste ban (from 21 May 2026). The overview note that only 2024/3230 is missing from the translation is therefore incomplete.

IMO MSC.1/Circ.1475 (https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/OurWork/Safety/Documents/MSC.1%20Circ.1475.pdf) §5.1: 'The SOLAS regulations prescribe two methods ... 5.1.1 Method No.1: Upon the conclusion of packing and sealing a container, the shipper may weigh, or have arranged that a third party weighs, the packed container. 5.1.2 Method No.2: The shipper ... may weigh all packages and cargo items, including the mass of pallets, dunnage and other packing and securing material to be packed in the container, and add the tare mass of the container to the sum of the single masses using a certified method'; §1.1 'In the absence of the shipper providing the verified gross mass of the packed container, the container should not be loaded on to the ship unless the master or his representative and the terminal representative have obtained the verified gross mass through other means'; §16.1 SOLAS VI/2 VGM requirements enter into force July 2016 (MSC.380(94), 1 July 2016). The same ctu-library.js chapter already says 'VGM은 적입 계획 단계의 추정값으로 대신할 수 없습니다(IM3 §1.1.7.3)', so the reworded 'estimated value at the packing-plan stage' matches. The 11 existing VGM mentions do not describe Methods 1 and 2.

MSC.1/Circ.1497 (CTU Code, 16 Dec 2014) §5.5 table: A = 'Baltic Sea (incl. Kattegat), Mediterranean Sea, Black Sea, Red Sea, Persian Gulf; Coastal or inter-island voyages in following areas: Central Atlantic Ocean (between 30°N and 35°S), Central Indian Ocean (down to 35°S), Central Pacific Ocean (between 30°N and 35°S)'; B = 'North Sea, Skagerak, English Channel, Sea of Japan, Sea of Okhotsk; Coastal or inter-island voyages ... South-Central Pacific Ocean (between 35°S and 45°S)'; C = 'unrestricted' (text of the IMO circular; the table is already transcribed at ctu-library.js lines 129-131). The Yellow Sea and East China Sea are not named. Shanghai (~31°N), Busan (~35°N) and Tokyo (~35.6°N) lie north of 30°N, so these routes are outside A's Central Pacific coastal band, and treating them as C follows the doc's own rule ('해역을 확인할 수 없으면 해상 C'). Correction: '한국 출발 항로라면 표에 이름이 나오는 곳은 동해뿐' is too broad. The Sea of Okhotsk (B) is also named and is relevant to Russian Far East routes, and long-haul routes cross named A seas (Red Sea, Mediterranean) although they are ocean voyages and therefore C. The edit is narrowed to 'near Korea', and the reason for C (north of 30°N, outside the A band) is added.
new: 해역(발트해·지중해·북해·동해 등)과, 지정된 대양 구역의 연안·도서 간 항해만 A·B로 낮출 수 있습니다. 한국 근해에서 표에 이름이 나오는 곳은 동해(Sea of Japan, B)뿐입니다(러시아 극동행이면 오호츠크해도 B). 부산~상하이·칭다오(황해·동중국해)나 부산~도쿄(일본 태평양 연안)처럼 표에 이름이 없는 해역을 지나는 항로는, 북위 30° 이북이라 A의 태평양 연안 항해 구간에도 들지 않으므로 해상 C로 계산하는 것이 안전합니다.
